title: Directing the band for acts at the Apollo and quitting unpaid
summary: Basie made Clayton conduct the band for acts at the Apollo, Baltimore and Washington, and he refused to continue because he got blame and no extra pay.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: And then we ran into that so many times later, like in the Apollo. We would get these acrobats and everything has got to be right down the line. And Basie would put me on the spot. I was out in the front of the band with the stick.
So if anything went wrong I got blamed for it. (LAUGHTER). Shuh.
Well that's an, it's almost an art in itself isn't it? I mean as distinct from playing for dancing?
Because the timing has got to be exactly right.
Yes. But I used to, I could direct, pretty good, from China. When I said we used to play one or two hours of light classical music.

And they were following me with the stick. I mean, if I didn't do something everything would go on. But it's a different thing playing for acts and jugglers when the tempo has got to break right here and then you go into something else.

But I was, I could direct pretty good. But I didn't appreciate that being out there. Especially on a Friday morning. That's when everybody used to go to the Apollo Theater. Smoke pot all the way back from the front seat.
Pot would come all up on the stage. And guys would stay up all Thursday night to be at that Apollo Theater the next morning, they knew Basie was coming.
And Basie put a big box out there and I was way up on top and this was for the acts and Basie wouldn't show up until it was time to do the

band number. And that was my job and I quit shortly because Basie didn't pay me for it. (LAUGHTER). We had a big argument about that. So you know, I'd done it three times. I did it in the Apollo, I did it in Baltimore, I did it in Washington.
And the next time we were coming back to Apollo, Basie hasn't said one word about giving me anything extra for directing and I get all the blame if everything goes wrong.

So, I told him, I said, you know one thing I'm not going to go back in the Apollo Theater. And so he got mad about it, but I didn't go back. I didn't go back and he never did pay me. Not until today he hasn't paid me for that.
What do you mean, oh, you didn't go back to conducting?
